# Best Open-Ear Earbuds for Running

## Top picks

**1. Bose Ultra Open Earbuds: best overall (~$199, down from $299)**
- Runner's World's top pick after 2,200+ logged miles. Testers found they don't bounce, work with hats and glasses, and leak less sound than most open designs. [Runner's World](https://www.runnersworld.com/gear/g63667125/best-open-ear-headphones-for-running/)
- WIRED says they have clearer sound than most competitors, and their physical buttons are easier to use mid-run than touch controls. [WIRED](https://www.wired.com/story/best-open-earbuds/)
- **Downsides:** They're only IPX4 and last about 7 to 7.5 hours per charge. They can also feel a bit quiet in heavy traffic.
- **Timing:** Runner's World says Bose plans to release new open-ear earbuds within about a month. If you're not in a hurry, you could wait for those or for a deeper discount on this model.
- Where to buy: the [Runner's World](https://www.runnersworld.com/gear/g63667125/best-open-ear-headphones-for-running/) and [WIRED](https://www.wired.com/story/best-open-earbuds/) guides link to Bose, Amazon, and Best Buy.

**2. Shokz OpenRun Pro 2: best bone conduction (~$125 on sale, $180 list)**
- This is the choice if hearing traffic matters most, since it leaves your ears completely open.
- It has 12-hour battery life, IP55 sweat resistance, physical buttons, and USB-C charging. [WIRED review](https://www.wired.com/review/review-shokz-openrun-pro-2/)
- It's bassier than older Shokz models, but less clear than the Bose.
- **Downsides:** The neckband can clash with ponytails, hoods, and high collars.
- **Price:** WIRED lists it at $125 at REI and Best Buy, and Runner's World saw $125 at Walmart. That's much better than paying $180.

**3. Shokz OpenDots 2: best for long runs and rain (~$200)**
- WIRED's overall #1 pick, and Runner's World's pick for long runs.
- It gets 10 hours per charge (40 with the case). Its IP57 rating is the strongest water resistance in either guide, and WIRED's reviewer fully submerged them with no problems. [WIRED](https://www.wired.com/story/best-open-earbuds/)

**4. Nothing Ear (Open): best mid-price (~$99, down from $149)**
- SoundGuys calls it the best workout earbud for running. It has strong bass for an open design, IP54, and a detailed EQ in its app. [SoundGuys](https://www.soundguys.com/best-workout-earbuds-2719/)
- Where to buy: [SoundGuys' open-ear guide](https://www.soundguys.com/best-open-ear-headphones-and-earbuds-115102/) links to Amazon.

## Budget options

**Soundcore AeroFit 2**
- SoundGuys' budget pick, with an ear-hook fit, IP55, and 10 hours per charge.
- **Price:** SoundGuys listed it at **$79.99 on Amazon** ([source](https://www.soundguys.com/best-open-ear-headphones-and-earbuds-115102/)), but that listing is from January, so check the current price.
- A deal site, Dealectric, shows $129.99 at Soundcore's own store, or about $104 with code AFSC20. The code doesn't work on items already on sale. Their link is an affiliate link, meaning they earn a commission if you buy. [Dealectric](https://dealectric.com/soundcore-aerofit-2)
- Amazon looks cheaper, so compare before you buy.

**JLab Flex Open (~$40)**
- An inexpensive way to find out whether you like clip-on earbuds at all. The sound is basic, but they're comfortable and stable. [Runner's World](https://www.runnersworld.com/gear/g63667125/best-open-ear-headphones-for-running/)

## Quick guidance
- **Road running in traffic:** Shokz OpenRun Pro 2
- **Best sound and comfort:** Bose Ultra Open (or wait for the new model)
- **Rain, sweat, or marathon-length runs:** Shokz OpenDots 2
- **Under $100:** Nothing Ear (Open) or Soundcore AeroFit 2

If you tell me your budget, whether you run in rain, and whether you wear hats or glasses, I can narrow this down to one pick.
